name: Duskrow Moto Jacket
description:
A motorcycle jacket built for the Gray Zone and lower Tier 2, where looking hard is sometimes the only armor you've got. The Duskrow is made from bonded synth-hide — not leather, not pretending to be — in a flat, worn-in black with faint horizontal ribbing across the shoulders and forearms. The cut is boxy enough to move in, with an asymmetric zip closure, two chest pockets with snap flaps, and a wide lapel collar that can be turned up against the wind off the lake. Pre-scuffed at the elbows. That's not a flaw. That's the design.

People who wear the Duskrow aren't trying to impress anyone at a Tier 3 wine bar. They're couriers, fixers, gig workers who ride secondhand mopeds through the Gray Zone's cracked-asphalt corridors. The jacket shows up in markets, in dive bars, in the back of dispatch vans. It holds its shape after a fall. It doesn't crack in the cold. It's the kind of jacket you hand down.
what_it_says: You don't have much, but you've got a code — and you've been around long enough that the jacket shows it.
story_hooks: A jacket matching this description was worn by the only witness to a the Gray Zone-level corporate dump — now someone is buying up every Duskrow in that colorway from secondhand stalls, looking for the right one.
The original Duskrow factory in the Gray Zone burned down six years ago; what's sold now is knockoffs of knockoffs, but an original pre-fire jacket has cult status among collectors.
A courier dies wearing one and the jacket ends up in a lost-and-found bin — the inside lining has a name and a locker number stitched into it.

physical_description.visual_profile: A brutalist moto silhouette with squared shoulders and a slight forward lean. The jacket reads aggressive without pretense—boxy, utilitarian, designed for function over fashion. Worn-in from day one, it sits on the body like a second skin that's already been through something.
physical_description.fit: Boxy and relaxed through the torso with tapered sleeves. Cut wide enough for layering and movement, but structured at the shoulders. Sits just past the hip.
physical_description.primary_material: Bonded synth-hide — a petroleum-based composite engineered to mimic leather's durability without the biological variance. Matte finish, no sheen.
physical_description.texture: Flat, slightly waxy surface with subtle horizontal ribbing across shoulders and forearms. Pre-scuffed elbows showing faint micro-tears in the weave. Surface has a worn-in grain despite being new—intentional distressing that reads as earned.
physical_description.color_scheme: Flat black throughout with no contrast stitching. The distressing reveals slightly lighter gray synth-hide beneath the surface scuffs. No logos or branding visible.
physical_description.closures: Asymmetric full-length zip running left-shoulder to right-hip. Two snap-flap chest pockets. No collar snaps—lapels fold freely.
distinctive_features: Horizontal ribbing texture across shoulders and forearms
Pre-scuffed elbows as intentional design detail
Wide lapel collar designed to flip up
No visible branding or Duskrow marks
physical_description.tier_indicator: Lower Tier 2 / Upper Tier 3 — expensive enough to signal investment, cheap enough to not fear losing it
physical_description.cultural_context: Courier culture, gig economy workers, the Gray Zone riders. The jacket says: 'I work for a living, I've eaten concrete, I don't need validation.' Street credibility without affectation.
physical_description.condition_typical: Broken-in immediately. Scuffs deepen with wear. Minor tears at stress points become badges. Never looks pristine; always looks reliable.
